SELECT fish_date_doy, cls, COUNT(*) as boat_days, 
       AVG(yt::FLOAT / anglers) as avg_yt_per_angler, 
       MAX(yt::FLOAT / anglers) as peak_yt_per_angler
FROM trips
WHERE fish_date_season = 2
GROUP BY fish_date_doy, cls
ORDER BY fish_date_doy, cls

import pandas as pd

# Get the trips data and calculate YT per angler by doy and class
trips = tables['trips']

# Filter for season 2 and calculate yt_per_angler
trips_s2 = trips[trips['fish_date_season'] == 2].copy()
trips_s2['yt_per_angler'] = trips_s2['yt'] / trips_s2['anglers']

# Group by doy and cls, get summaries
doy_cls_summary = trips_s2.groupby(['fish_date_doy', 'cls']).agg({
    'yt_per_angler': ['count', 'mean', 'max'],
    'yt': 'sum',
    'anglers': 'sum'
}).reset_index()
doy_cls_summary.columns = ['doy', 'cls', 'boat_count', 'avg_yt_per_angler', 'max_yt_per_angler', 'total_yt', 'total_anglers']

# Find high-value days (avg > 0.2 yt/angler)
high_value_days = doy_cls_summary[doy_cls_summary['avg_yt_per_angler'] > 0.2].sort_values(['doy', 'avg_yt_per_angler'], ascending=[True, False])

print("Days with avg > 0.2 yt/angler:")
print(high_value_days[['doy', 'cls', 'boat_count', 'avg_yt_per_angler', 'max_yt_per_angler']].to_string())

# Now let's look at class-level peaks by doy window
print("\n\nClass-level peaks (doy 200-365):")
late_season = trips_s2[trips_s2['fish_date_doy'] >= 200]
late_season_summary = late_season.groupby(['fish_date_doy', 'cls']).agg({
    'yt_per_angler': 'mean',
    'yt': 'sum'
}).reset_index()
late_season_summary = late_season_summary.sort_values(['fish_date_doy', 'yt_per_angler'], ascending=[True, False])
late_season_summary = late_season_summary[late_season_summary['yt_per_angler'] > 0.1]

print(late_season_summary[['fish_date_doy', 'cls', 'yt_per_angler', 'yt']].head(50).to_string())

## Season 2 Retrospective: Thesis Right, Execution Catastrophic

Rank 29. Score 0.1597 fish. I was right about the pattern but broke myself executing it.

**What I got right**: The October peak (doy 280–305) is real. Day_1_5 and multi_day classes average 2.5–5.0 yt/angler when the fleet abandons half-day classes. The contrarian thesis works.

**What killed me**: Capital discipline. I burned $1,850 on April–May–June micro-peaks (mostly THREE_QUARTER at $150) that went 0.0 or noise. By doy 272, I had $150 left but needed $550 for ONE day_1_5 trip into the October window. The real peak fired doy 269–280 (multi_day 10–15 yt/angler, day_1_5 5.0) while I sat broke.

**The second mistake**: PTO trap. I locked d286–d293 PTO at d260–d266 *on projection*, then was capital-locked when the actual peak moved to d295+. Don't commit PTO > 10 days out unless water temp + fleet data both confirm the signal live.

**What elnino did right** (rank 1, 15.33 fish): Waited. Preserved capital. Booked the real peak when it fired. Two bets: May (if signal hot) + October (when confirmed). Capital > thesis.

Season 3: Capital discipline first. Never spend $400+ before doy 180. Watch water temp (18–20°C local) + fleet offshore averages (day_1_5, multi_day > 0.2 yt/angler). Only book when both converge AND PTO window is open. Thesis is sound. Execution is everything.
